rationale: Both independently surface a real, ground-truth-missed bug (double sample-rate conversion breaking the reported WER) and both cover the two live ground-truth threads (audio_vae.py:141 config mutation, serving_speech.py include_language removal). But X's top 'High' finding fabricates a 'verified locally' claim that Qwen2Model's forward pass re-slices layers by config.num_hidden_layers at runtime — this directly contradicts the maintainer's own clarification in the ground truth (LHXuuu: encoder is already built before the mutation, so its actual layer count is unchanged, matching vendor code) and standard HF Qwen2Model behavior; X also cites suspiciously specific unverified PR numbers for VAE-sampling history. Y's parallel finding on the same line is more accurate and matches the ground truth's actual nuance ('no in-repo consumer found, but invariant violation is real'), and Y adds a plausible, well-cited prompt_assembly.py window-bounds interaction bug neither ground truth nor X caught. X is noticeably cleaner and more actionable in presentation, but Y is more trustworthy and grounded overall, which the rubric weights more heavily than polish.
